\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{برکت} (barkat)}{برکت (barkat)}]{\ur{برکت} (barkat) — a blessing; plenty}

\label{lesson:UR-C528-barkat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an excuse, then the Urdu for to get bored.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{برکت}}
\textbf{\ur{برکت}} — \emph{barkat} — \textquotedblleft{}a blessing; plenty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{بارش} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{کھیتوں} \ur{میں} \ur{برکت} \ur{ہو} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar bārish huī to khetoṅ meṅ barkat ho gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it rains, the fields will be blessed with plenty.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{برکت}} (\emph{barkat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{baraka}, \textquotedblleft{}a blessing, abundance\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barkat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barkat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar bārish huī to khetoṅ meṅ barkat ho gī.} — If it rains, the fields will be blessed with plenty.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an excuse, then the Urdu for to get bored, then say \emph{barkat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{برکت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A blessing; plenty\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ثواب} (savāb)}{ثواب (savāb)}]{\ur{ثواب} (savāb) — spiritual merit (for a good deed)}

\label{lesson:UR-C528-savab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to get bored, then the Urdu for a blessing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ثواب}}
\textbf{\ur{ثواب}} — \emph{savāb} — \textquotedblleft{}spiritual merit (for a good deed)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{مدد} \ur{کرتے} \ur{ہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{ثواب} \ur{ملتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp madad karte haiṅ to savāb miltā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you help someone, you earn merit.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ثواب}} (\emph{savāb}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{thawāb}, \textquotedblleft{}a reward\textquotedblright{}, especially for a good deed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{savāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{savāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp madad karte haiṅ to savāb miltā hai.} — If you help someone, you earn merit.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to get bored, then the Urdu for a blessing, then say \emph{savāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ثواب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Spiritual merit (for a good deed)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تعویذ} (tāvīz)}{تعویذ (tāvīz)}]{\ur{تعویذ} (tāvīz) — an amulet}

\label{lesson:UR-C528-taviz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a blessing, then the Urdu for spiritual merit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تعویذ}}
\textbf{\ur{تعویذ}} — \emph{tāvīz} — \textquotedblleft{}an amulet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{دادی} \ur{ہوتیں} \ur{تو} \ur{بچے} \ur{کو} \ur{تعویذ} \ur{دیتیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar dādī hotīṅ to bachche ko tāvīz detīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If grandmother were here, she would give the child an amulet.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تعویذ}} (\emph{tāvīz}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taʿwīdh}, \textquotedblleft{}seeking protection\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for saying what happens if.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نذرانہ} (nazrānā)}{نذرانہ (nazrānā)}]{\ur{نذرانہ} (nazrānā) — an offering (to someone revered)}

\label{lesson:UR-C528-nazrana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for spiritual merit, then the Urdu for an amulet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نذرانہ}}
\textbf{\ur{نذرانہ}} — \emph{nazrānā} — \textquotedblleft{}an offering (to someone revered)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ہم} \ur{استاد} \ur{کے} \ur{گھر} \ur{گئے} \ur{تو} \ur{نذرانہ} \ur{دیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ham ustād ke ghar gae to nazrānā deṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we go to our teacher's house, we will make an offering.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نذرانہ}} (\emph{nazrānā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{nazrāna}, built on Arabic \emph{nadhr}, \textquotedblleft{}a vow, an offering\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazrānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazrānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar ham ustād ke ghar gae to nazrānā deṅ ge.} — If we go to our teacher's house, we will make an offering.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for spiritual merit, then the Urdu for an amulet, then say \emph{nazrānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{نذرانہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An offering (to someone revered)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نوازنا} (navāznā)}{نوازنا (navāznā)}]{\ur{نوازنا} (navāznā) — to bestow favour on; to honour}

\label{lesson:UR-C528-navazna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an amulet, then the Urdu for an offering.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نوازنا}}
\textbf{\ur{نوازنا}} — \emph{navāznā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bestow favour on; to honour\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{خدا} \ur{نے} \ur{نوازا} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{نیا} \ur{گھر} \ur{بنائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar khudā ne navāzā to ham nayā ghar banāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we are blessed, we will build a new house.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{مہمان} \ur{کو} \ur{تحفے} \ur{سے} \ur{نوازا}, \emph{us ne mehmān ko tohfe se navāzā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نوازنا}} (\emph{navāznā}) is built on Persian \emph{navāz-}, usually traced to the present stem of \emph{navākhtan}, \textquotedblleft{}to caress, to favour\textquotedblright{}, with the Urdu verb ending \emph{-nā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{navāznā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{navāznā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar khudā ne navāzā to ham nayā ghar banāeṅ ge.} — If we are blessed, we will build a new house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an amulet, then the Urdu for an offering, then say \emph{navāznā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{نوازنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To bestow favour on; to honour\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
